body:
UI/UX review of head `669c595aa`, from sn3ro (Claude Code), as qsmits asked on #4245. This is a contributor's pre-check, not a collaborator review.

## What I ran

- A local build of `669c595aa` (detached worktree, no change pushed).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- pane_fold layout_shell`: 12 passed, 0 failed.
- On the earlier head `485c9d934`, three tests of `pane_fold` failed with `Harness::run exceeded max_steps`. The repaint came from `shell.rs:158` on each frame. `669c595aa` ("the fold hold asks for a frame only on a change") fixes it. I confirm that it passes now.
- Local screenshots at 1366 × 768 from `ShellUi::seeded()` (a temporary `#[ignore]` test that I did not push).

| All panes open | Both side panes folded |
|---|---|
| ![open](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/4492-review/open.png) | ![folded](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/4492-review/folded.png) |

## What is good

- The folded pane is a flat docked strip with a hairline, not a floating pill. This agrees with research note 3. The turned title reads well, and the ▶ arrow above it tells how to unfold.
- The viewport takes the full width, and the strips stay at the window edges.
- One flag (`LeafNode::collapsed`) for the arrow, the setups and the fold law is a good choice. The mark `camcraft_pane_folds` keeps older setups loading.
- Layout stays view state: no command and no history entry.

## Findings

1. **The chip tooltip shows far from the pointer.** With the pointer at the centre of the Browser chip (y ≈ 425), "Unfold Browser" is painted at y ≈ 741, over the status bar:

   ![tooltip](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/4492-review/tip-crop.png)

   Cause: egui puts a tooltip under the rect of the widget, and the chip is as high as the pane. Fix: in `camcraft_ui_kit::fold::fold_chip`, use `resp.on_hover_text_at_pointer(label)` in place of `resp.on_hover_text(label)`.

2. **The hover state of the chip is not visible in the dark theme.** The fill changes from `ink_alt` `#2C3037` to `field_hover` `#2A2E35` (measured on the render: (44,48,55) to (42,46,53)). The contrast between the two is about 1.03:1, so a user sees no change. In the light theme the change is visible (`#F6F7F9` to `#DDE1E7`). Proposal: on hover, keep the fill and paint the title in `text` with a 1 px `accent` hairline on the inner edge, or use a token with a clear step in both themes. The kit test can check the step with `contrast.rs`.

3. **A folded side pane hides the safety state, and nothing else shows it yet.** In the folded screenshot, the "OK · 105 moves · 4 warnings" line and the warning glyph of Contour1 are gone. The status bar shows only "1 Operation". The body of #4245 (E2) says: "Each chip keeps the safety state as text. The Browser chip shows the counts of failed and stale operations. The Properties chip shows the state of the operation." The decision of 2026-11-28 moved the counts to the folded issues line, but PR I (the issues pane) does not exist yet. Until it does, a user who folds the Browser does not see that operations need a regenerate. Proposal, one of these:
   - (a) this PR shows a short state under the title in the chip (for example "2 stale" on the Browser chip, "Needs regenerate" on the Properties chip), from `status_of`, as text with a glyph;
   - (b) a follow-up issue, linked to #4245 and to PR I, that says when this gap closes. PR P and PR I then ship in the same cut.

   I recommend (a) for the Properties chip at minimum, because the state of the open operation is one call.

4. **The fold arrow of the viewport does nothing.** The viewport leaf still shows ▼, and a click on it does nothing, because the fold law clears the flag (`the_viewport_never_folds`). Before this PR, the arrow on a side pane also did nothing, so the dead arrow was not noticed. Now that the arrow works on the side panes, the dead one on the viewport looks like a fault. egui_dock 0.21 has only the global switch `show_leaf_collapse_buttons`, so the arrow cannot be hidden on one leaf. There are two ways:
   - hide all arrows and give the side panes a fold control of our own (the decision file dropped this option for cost);
   - keep the arrows, and write in `docs/decisions/4483-pane-fold.md` why the viewport arrow stays and does nothing.

   At a minimum, do the second.

5. **Small: a separator drag on a folded pane snaps back.** The test `a_separator_drag_does_not_unfold_a_folded_pane` checks that the width does not change, which is correct. But during the drag the separator still shows the drag cursor and the pane moves, then jumps back on the next frame. This is acceptable for this PR. A note in the decision file is enough.

6. **Nit:** the module doc of `crates/ui/src/egui_app/layout/setups.rs` has one line of about 150 characters ("...loads with every pane unfolded. Provenance: our own code, ..."). Wrap it as the lines around it.

## Not checked

- The light theme render (I checked only the token values).
- A fold inside a floating window (the body says that a float keeps the egui_dock behaviour).
- The camera: E2 says "The camera does not move when a pane folds or opens". I did not measure the view centre before and after a fold. A test could compare the projected position of the WCS origin before and after.

Findings 1 and 2 are small kit changes. Finding 3 is the one that matters most for safety: a CAM user must not lose the stale state when a pane folds.

Thank you, sn3ro. The review is clear, and the screenshots make each point easy to check. We take all six findings into this PR before it is flagged ready:

1. The tooltip goes to the pointer (`on_hover_text_at_pointer`).
2. The hover gets a step that is visible in both themes, with a contrast test in the kit.
3. Agreed, this is the important one. Both chips keep the safety state as text with a glyph: the Browser chip shows the counts of stale and failed operations, and the Properties chip shows the state of the open operation ("Up to date" / "Needs regenerate"). We do not wait for PR I.
4. The dead viewport arrow is documented in the decision file, or hidden if there is a clean way.
5. The snap-back during a separator drag is noted in the decision file.
6. The long doc line is wrapped.

We also add a test that a fold does not move the camera, if it is cheap.
